themes_detail.label: Lead contamination spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints surged to 19 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 4.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 347% spike (z-score: 5.6)—suggesting either a new environmental hazard, renovation-related disturbance, or increased resident awareness in Crown Heights/Prospect Heights.
evidence: 19 lead complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (347% increase; z-score: 5.6)
476 total DOB building permits filed in last 90 days, including 272 alteration filings that may expose lead paint
Community board budget request for 'additional building inspectors' suggests chronic capacity gap in lead enforcement
reporting_angles: Which buildings or blocks are generating the lead complaints? Are they tied to renovation activity?
Interview residents in affected buildings about symptoms and remediation timelines; contact NYC Health for lead testing availability

themes_detail.label: Noise from houses of worship
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from houses of worship exploded to 4 THIS WEEK, a 3100% spike versus a baseline of 0.1 complaints per week over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72)—the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset—pointing to a specific, acute conflict in the neighborhood.
evidence: 4 noise complaints from houses of worship THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (3100% increase; z-score: 11.72, highest spike in dataset)
Crown Heights has historically diverse religious institutions (Orthodox Jewish, Muslim, Christian congregations) in close residential proximity
No prior Reddit discussion or CB data on this issue, suggesting newly surfaced or rapid escalation
reporting_angles: Which specific house(s) of worship are generating complaints this week? What triggered the sudden increase?
Interview both complainants and affected congregations; consult NYPD noise enforcement and CB 308 on any mediation efforts

themes_detail.label: Tree damage and disease cluster
themes_detail.summary: Over THIS WEEK, dead/dying trees (6 complaints vs. 0.5 baseline, 1100% spike) and overgrown branches (7 complaints vs. 0.8 baseline, 833% spike) converged with a new tree request surge (6 complaints last week vs. 0.4 baseline, 1500% spike)—indicating possible storm damage, disease outbreak, or maintenance failure affecting streetscape health.
evidence: Dead/dying trees: 6 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (1100% increase; z-score: 11.0)
Overgrown tree/branches: 7 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (833% increase; z-score: 9.45)
New tree requests: 6 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (1500% increase; z-score: 8.08)
Community board budget repeatedly requests 'reconstruct or upgrade a building in a park'—suggests infrastructure strain
reporting_angles: Did a recent storm (wind, heavy rain) cause the spike? Consult NYC Parks and weather data for confirmation.
Are specific parks or blocks disproportionately affected? Map the complaints geographically; interview Parks Department on maintenance backlog

themes_detail.label: Elevator failures in rental buildings
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped to 3 LAST WEEK, a 700% spike versus a baseline of 0.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.42)—concerning in a neighborhood with significant multi-family housing stock where elevator outages trap residents and pose accessibility risks.
evidence: 3 elevator complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase; z-score: 5.42)
476 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days suggest active alteration and renovation work that may disrupt elevators
No corresponding spike in door/window complaints (DOWN 71% this week), limiting confounding factors
reporting_angles: Which buildings are experiencing elevator outages? How long have residents been without service?
Interview elderly and disabled residents about impact; contact DOB on violations issued; examine whether landlords are deferring maintenance

themes_detail.label: Missing street signage
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints spiked to 3 reports three weeks ago, a 1100% increase versus the baseline of 0.2 per week (z-score: 6.35)—a signal that has already begun to cool but may indicate wayfinding or traffic safety degradation in need of verification.
evidence: 3 missing street sign complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% increase; z-score: 6.35)
Signal is older than other spikes and may reflect transient event rather than ongoing pattern
Community board budget requests park and building improvements, but no specific street signage mention
reporting_angles: Were signs stolen, vandalized, or removed during construction? Are specific corridors or intersections affected?
Verify current status of sign replacements with DOT; assess whether spike has subsided
